chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prey of a falcon when it hunts and kills and eats from it — may I eat from its remainder or not? So he (peace be upon him) said: As for what the bird ate, do not eat (from it), unless you slaughter it (properly).

key_terms.الْبَازِي: al-bazi: the falcon, a bird of prey used in falconry (sayd al-jawariḥ); falconry was common among Arabs and Persians and is explicitly mentioned in Quran 5:4
key_terms.تُذَكِّيَهُ: tadhkiyah: ritual purification/slaughter; the act of invoking God's name and slaughtering the animal properly to make it lawful for consumption
key_terms.صَيْد: sayd: hunting/prey; in fiqh refers to game animals caught through hunting
key_terms.فَضْل: fadl: remainder/leftover; what remains after the hunting bird has eaten its portion

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the remainder of prey that a falcon has hunted and partially eaten?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the permissibility of consuming prey caught by a trained falcon when the bird has eaten part of the catch. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the portion eaten by the falcon becomes impermissible for human consumption unless the remaining animal is ritually slaughtered (tadhkiyah). This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential principle that the act of tadhkiyah (proper Islamic slaughter) is a prerequisite for the lawfulness of meat, and the falcon's consumption does not substitute for this requirement.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a prey of the falcon when it hunts, and kills, and eats from it – can one eat from its remainder or not?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for what the bird ate, so do not eat, except if you purify (slaughter) it’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ’Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the hunting of falcons which it catches and eats thereof; if the remaining can be used for food.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever birds eat do not use it for food unless you slaughter it properly.’”
